fi-leporinus-fasciatus.title: Banded Leporinus
fi-leporinus-fasciatus.summary: The banded leporinus, Leporinus fasciatus, is an anostomid from the Amazon and Orinoco systems and coastal Guyana, Suriname and French Guiana. Young fish are often sold without warning of their size…
rows: groups of 6 or more in larger tanks, but otherwise keep just a single specimen in a community of peaceful medium to large fishes.
This species was described from Suriname but no specific locality was given.
notes: Décor is relatively unimportant and maintenance simple provided sufficient space is available and oxygenation adequate.
A natural-style arrangement could consist of a sandy substrate with some leaf litter plus large driftwood branches and twisted roots.

fi-chalceus-macrolepidotus.title: Pink Tail Chalceus
fi-chalceus-macrolepidotus.summary: The pink-tailed chalceus, Chalceus macrolepidotus, is a large characin found throughout northern South America, from Colombia to French Guiana. It inhabits the surface layers of highly oxygenated…
rows: Usually kept singly (or a known pair when breeding)
Feeds primarily on insects and aquatic crustaceans in nature.
Found throughout northern South America in Colombia, Venezuela, Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana and Peru.
notes: It requires a lot of swimming space, so decor is not really critical, although a sandy substrate with some beech branches and floating plants looks very effective, and mimics many of its natural biotopes.
The floating cover will also help to reduce bouts of skittishness, to which it is prone.

fi-ctenolucius-hujeta.title: Silver Gar SA
fi-ctenolucius-hujeta.summary: The gar characin, Ctenolucius hujeta, is a predatory pike characid from the Lake Maracaibo basin in Venezuela west to the Río Sinú in Colombia. Also traded as 'freshwater barracuda' and 'hujeta gar',…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates
Schooling / social — keep a proper group
An obligate predator feeding mostly on smaller fishes and insects in nature but in most cases adapting well to dead alternatives in captivity.
It's natural range extends west from the Lake Maracaibo basin of northwestern Venezuela via the Río Magdalena drainage in northern Colombia as far as the Río Sinú in the northwest…
notes: This species is a near-exclusive inhabitant of the upper water column and appreciates surface cover in the form of floating or overhanging vegetation.
Other décor is relatively unimportant but can consist of a sandy substrate with leaf litter plus some large driftwood branches and twisted roots.

fi-nannostomus-beckfordi.title: Red Beckfords Pencilfish
fi-nannostomus-beckfordi.summary: The golden pencilfish, Nannostomus beckfordi, is a lebiasinid widely distributed across Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana, Brazil and Venezuela. The type species of the genus and fairly ubiquitous in…
rows: Predator / carnivore. A micropredator feeding on tiny invertebrates and other zooplankton in nature.
Type locality is 'Goedverwagting, a plantation on the Coast of Demerara, Guyana ' but this species is widely-distributed throughout rivers of Guyana, Suriname, and French Guiana…
notes: Should ideally be kept in a heavily-planted set-up, preferably with a dark substrate.
The broken lines of sight that exist in such a display allow it to display natural behaviour as well as helping to reduce skittishness.

fi-leporinus-nijsseni.title: Spotted Leporinus
fi-leporinus-nijsseni.summary: A gold, black-spotted headstander from Suriname. One of the calmer Leporinus, it grazes plant foods and does well in a roomy community of similar-sized fish.
rows: Peaceful for a Leporinus; may eat small shrimp, crabs or crayfish
Mostly plant-based: spirulina or algae wafers and vegetables, with occasional meaty foods. May nibble soft plants
Saramacca Creek and Suriname River basins, Suriname
warn: Strong jumper: needs a tight-fitting lid.
